title: Growing or Shrinking: Which Southeast Asian Races Are Gaining and Losing Finishers
seo_title: Southeast Asian Races Growing or Shrinking: Finisher Trends
meta_description: Finisher counts for 31 Southeast Asian races against earlier editions: Manila and Hanoi growing fast, Laguna Phuket shrinking, and runners moving up from the 10K to the half.
dek: Comparing official results year on year shows which races are pulling in more runners and which are losing them. The Manila Marathon has grown thirteenfold at the marathon distance in two years; Laguna Phuket's marathon field is a quarter of its 2019 size. Here is what 83 editions of 35 races show, and where the numbers need care.

sections.heading: What is being compared
paragraphs: Run SEA keeps the official results of 75 recent races and an archive of earlier editions for 35 of them: 52 past editions with 199,099 finishers, going back as far as 2019 [1]. For 31 races, the archive has at least one earlier edition to set against the latest one. The counts here are finishers in the 10K, half marathon and marathon, as listed by the timing company. They are not entries, and 5K, fun-run and other distances are not counted.

Taken together, those 31 races had 88,050 finishers at their previous edition and 93,546 at their latest, up 6% [1]. That headline is almost entirely the Manila Marathon. Without it, the other 30 races went from 73,668 finishers to 72,702, down 1%, and 15 of the 31 races grew while 16 shrank.

sections.heading: Runners are moving up a distance
paragraphs: The clearest pattern is not in totals but in distances. In the 30 races that held a 10K at both editions, 10K finishers fell 13%, from 46,172 to 40,088. In the 29 with a half marathon at both, half-marathon finishers rose 21%, from 34,531 to 41,628. In the eight with a marathon at both, marathon finishers rose 37%, from 7,347 to 10,060, although the Manila Marathon supplies most of that rise [1].

The PUMA Philippine Half Marathon Series shows it most cleanly. At its Cagayan de Oro, Cebu and Clark legs, total finishers barely changed between 2025 and 2026, but the half marathon went from 470 to 1,100, from 445 to 1,125 and from 881 to 1,356, while the 10K fell by a similar number at each [1]. The same runners, or the same number of them, chose the longer race.

sections.heading: The risers
paragraphs: The Manila Marathon is the fastest-growing race in the archive. Its marathon had 431 finishers in October 2024, 2,827 in August 2025 and 5,744 in June 2026. Across all three distances it went from 4,421 to 14,382 to 20,844 finishers in two years [1].
The PUMA series' Manila leg nearly doubled, from 5,135 finishers in 2025 to 9,751 in 2026, with the half marathon rising from 2,371 to 6,166 [1].

Vietnam's races are growing steadily. Techcombank Hanoi International Marathon went from 5,479 finishers in 2024 to 8,607 in 2025 and 9,491 in 2026, and its marathon field from 1,110 to 1,975. VPBank Dat Sen Hong Music Marathon in Dong Thap went from 1,412 finishers in 2022 and 2,827 in 2023 to 5,997 in 2026, and Garmin Run Vietnam from 3,608 to 4,839 in a year [1].
In Indonesia, Crystalin Run Xperience in Jakarta grew from 1,890 to 2,934 finishers, with its half marathon more than doubling from 494 to 1,069 [1].

sections.heading: The fallers
paragraphs: Laguna Phuket Marathon has the longest record in the archive and the clearest long decline. Its marathon had 2,231 finishers in 2019, 1,049 in 2022, 979 in 2023, 851 in 2024, 595 in 2025 and 603 in 2026. The half marathon fell from 3,689 in 2019 to 1,737 [1]. The race as a whole grew 19% between 2025 and 2026, helped by a 10K, which appears in the archive only from 2024, but its headline distance is a quarter of its pre-pandemic size.
Khun Dan Marathon, at the Khun Dan Prakan Chon Dam in Nakhon Nayok [2], had 3,132 finishers in 2019, 1,599 in 2024, 2,232 in 2025 and 1,880 in 2026 [1].

In the Philippines, Discovery Marathon fell from 1,687 finishers to 971, with its marathon halving from 471 to 230. Isla del Fuego Marathon on Siquijor went from 1,528 in 2024 to 2,915 in 2025 and back to 1,766 in 2026. HOKA Midnight Run's Cebu leg fell from 2,138 to 1,049, and Takbo para sa Kalikasan has fallen each year, from 3,907 to 2,775 to 2,422 [1].

The steepest drops are at the five city races of the Sante Barley Trilogy Run Asia's third leg in Manila, Cebu, Cagayan de Oro, Davao and Iloilo, down between 61% and 83% from 2025 in the half marathon and 10K. That needs the biggest caveat of all: each city's third leg in 2026 was headlined by a 32 km [2], which is not in either year's count, so these figures may show runners moving to the 32K rather than leaving the race.

sections.heading: Why to read these numbers carefully
paragraphs: Finishers are not entrants. A hot morning, a tight cut-off or a course problem cuts the finisher count without anyone staying away. Results pages can also be incomplete, and a timing company may publish some categories separately or not at all.

Dates and distances move. The Manila Marathon ran in October, then August, then June, so its editions were 8 to 10 months apart. Several races added or dropped distances between editions: The archive holds only 10K results for EastWest Dream Run's 2025 Manila race and for Gemadept Run's 2024 and 2025 editions in Ho Chi Minh City, while both have a half marathon in 2026 [1], so part of their growth is a new distance.
One year is not a trend. Most of the 31 comparisons cover two editions, and a race can lose runners one year and win them back the next, as the swings at Isla del Fuego and Khun Dan show.

sections.heading: Using this when choosing a race
paragraphs: A growing race usually means a busier start, longer queues at packet pick-up and bag drop, and more company on the course. A shrinking one can mean a quieter, easier race day. Neither is better; it depends on what you want from the morning.

Some of the biggest fields in the archive have no latest edition to compare yet. Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok had 38,098 finishers across its marathon, half and 10K in 2025, the largest single race in our data. Borobudur Marathon had 10,357, Halong Bay Heritage Marathon 8,072 and the AIA Rock 'n' Roll Running Series Manila 5,860 [1]. Their next editions will show which way they are heading, and the page of each upcoming race on runsea.run shows its last edition's field.

faqs.question: Which Southeast Asian races are growing fastest?
faqs.answer: In Run SEA's results archive, the Manila Marathon grew from 4,421 finishers in 2024 to 20,844 in 2026, and its marathon from 431 to 5,744. The PUMA Half Marathon Series' Manila leg, Techcombank Hanoi, VPBank Dat Sen Hong in Dong Thap and Garmin Run Vietnam also grew strongly.

faqs.question: Is Laguna Phuket Marathon getting smaller?
faqs.answer: Its marathon has. The marathon had 2,231 finishers in 2019 and has fallen at almost every edition since, to 603 in 2026, while the half fell from 3,689 to 1,737. The event as a whole grew 19% from 2025 to 2026, helped by its 10K.

faqs.question: Are more runners in Southeast Asia moving up to the half marathon?
faqs.answer: Across 29 races with a half marathon at two editions, half-marathon finishers rose 21% while 10K finishers at 30 races fell 13%. At the PUMA series' Cagayan de Oro, Cebu and Clark legs, totals held steady while runners shifted from the 10K to the half.

editorial_notes: New 6 Nov 2026. Built from data/finish-times (latest editions) and data/finish-times-history (52 earlier editions of 35 races, 199,099 finishers). Comparisons use each race's latest archived edition against its current file; counts are 10K, half and marathon finishers only (5K, fun runs and the Trilogy 32K are not in the data). Edition dates from the history files. Totals: 31 races, 88,050 to 93,546 (+6.2%); excluding Manila Marathon 73,668 to 72,702 (-1.3%). No external sources needed: every figure is our own data.
